title: Microsoft Teams: Security detections report in the Teams admin center
notes: claim 53: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the summary promises that no action is needed to receive the report, but Microsoft does not state its arrival default and the body acknowledges that uncertainty. The report paths, export details and roadmap facts are supported; the licensing field and the statement about non-configurable blocked file types also need qualification.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Teams admin center Security detections report centralises detections generated for Teams communications.
claims.quote: The Security detections report in the Microsoft Teams admin center helps you investigate security detections generated for Teams communications in your organization.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The report includes impersonation, malicious URL and weaponizable file detections generated by Teams security protections.
claims.quote: The report includes detections generated by Teams security protections, such as impersonation, malicious URL, and weaponizable file detections.

claims.claim: Admins can review potentially malicious conversations and investigate detection details.
claims.quote: This report provides a centralized view of security detections across Teams, enabling you to review potentially malicious conversations, investigate detection details, and export the results to a CSV file for further analysis.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Report results can be exported to CSV.
claims.quote: export the results to a CSV file for further analysis.

claims.claim: No action is required to receive the report.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report Teams automatically available enable report setting retention licensing. Opened the report and reporting reference; neither states an automatic arrival default. The body says Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival.
claims.fix: Replace 'no action is required to receive it' with 'Microsoft has not stated whether anything needs enabling'. Keep defaultState as unknown.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The report is reached in Teams admin center through Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > Security detections.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. On the View reports tab, under Report, select Security detections.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation for this report as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report PowerShell Microsoft Graph API; Teams PowerShell security detections report export FileTypeCheck. Read report, reporting reference, Teams messaging cmdlet, Graph security overview and Safe Attachments report excerpts; none documents this report's automation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Weaponizable File Protection is configured in Teams admin center under Messaging settings > Messaging safety > Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Messaging settings. Scroll down to Messaging safety settings. Turn on the setting: Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.

claims.claim: The Teams-module call Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCheck "Enabled" -Identity Global enables Weaponizable File Protection.
claims.quote: You can also configure file protection using PowerShell with the Teams module: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCheck "Enabled" -Identity Global

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls table; Risk assessment

claims.claim: The file-protection setting governs tenant-wide message protection rather than configuring the report.
claims.quote: Once enabled, all users in the tenant will have file protection applied to their Teams messages.

claims.claim: The Weaponizable File Protection page says the blocked file-type list is not currently configurable by administrators.

claims.fix: Replace the note's last sentence with: 'The feature page says the blocked file-type list is not configurable, but the PowerShell reference documents CustomBlockList with FileTypeBlockList for custom blocked types when FileTypeCheck is Enabled.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmessagingconfiguration?view=teams-ps.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the report's arrival default.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report default enable retention date range; Security detections report Teams automatically available enable report setting retention licensing. Opened report and reporting reference; neither states an arrival default or enabling prerequisite.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no requirement specific to this report is published.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams can be licensed as part of qualifying Microsoft 365 offerings or as a standalone SKU.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the notes with: 'Microsoft Teams is licensed through qualifying Microsoft 365 offerings or a standalone Teams SKU. A requirement specific to the Security detections report is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/teams-service-description. This records the product-level entitlement, not a claim that the report has a separately confirmed free entitlement.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to the Security detections report.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report license; Microsoft Teams admin center licensing requirements reports Teams license. Opened report, reporting reference and Teams service description; none names a report-specific licence. The service description supplies general Teams licensing.

claims.claim: The report's own Learn page lists no prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams security detections report licensing prerequisites meter price default automatically enable retention PowerShell Graph API export. Read the entire Security detections report page; it contains viewing instructions and report fields but no prerequisites section or prerequisite statement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The reporting reference names access roles but no licence for this report.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams admin center licensing requirements reports Teams license. Read the Teams reporting reference in full; its access section lists admin roles and its Security detections row lists availability and fields, but neither names a licence for this report.

claims.claim: No report-specific meter, price or spending cap is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams security detections report licensing prerequisites meter price default automatically enable retention PowerShell Graph API export. Read report, reporting reference and Teams service description; none names a report-specific meter, price or cap.

claims.claim: No autonomous action by the report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report anonymous conceal names FileTypeCheck setting autonomous price meter. Read report: it documents viewing, running and exporting reports and administrators using identifiers, not autonomous report actions.

claims.claim: Learn documents no setting of the report's own.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report Teams automatically available enable report setting retention licensing. Opened report, reporting reference and Teams messaging configuration reference; none identifies a report-specific configuration switch.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Leaving the report alone changes nothing about what Teams blocks.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report Teams automatically available enable report setting retention licensing. Read report and file-protection page; they document a reporting view and a separate protection setting, but do not state what leaving the report alone guarantees.
claims.fix: Replace 'The report is a view of detections, not a new protection, so leaving it alone changes nothing about what Teams blocks' with 'The report provides a view of detections generated by Teams security protections.'

claims.claim: Learn does not describe how the file-protection setting relates to the report.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report anonymous conceal names FileTypeCheck setting autonomous price meter; Teams PowerShell security detections report export FileTypeCheck. Read report, file-protection page and messaging reference; no text specifies how the setting affects report records.

claims.claim: The report page gives example date ranges but no maximum lookback or detection-record retention period.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report default enable retention date range. Read complete report and reporting reference; only Last 7 days and Last 30 days examples appear. Defender retention and Safe Attachments search results describe other datasets, not this report.

claims.claim: The applicability of concealed usage-report names to Security detections report is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report anonymous conceal names FileTypeCheck setting autonomous price meter. Read reporting reference and anonymous-names troubleshooting excerpts: they cover usage reports; neither explicitly covers this protection report.

claims.claim: The reporting reference names Teams user activity, device usage and usage reports for its concealed-names setting.
claims.quote: Enabling this setting de-identifies user, group, and site name information in the Teams user activity report, Teams device usage report, and Teams usage report.

claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to take stock of role assignments, but the controls table has no role-assignment row.
claims.quote: Confirm who holds the Teams administrator and Global reader roles ... Controls rows: Viewing and exporting security detections in Teams; Weaponizable File Protection.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Confirm who holds the Teams administrator and Global reader roles, since the Teams reporting reference names these roles for opening reports.' Keep the documented access roles in Scope and the report row note.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to block external senders, but the controls table has no external-sender blocking row.
claims.quote: Use the Sender MRI to block a repeat external sender on the External Access page ... Controls rows: Viewing and exporting security detections in Teams; Weaponizable File Protection.
claims.fix: Remove 'Use the Sender MRI to block a repeat external sender on the External Access page' from the After rollout checklist. Keep the supported explanation of Sender MRI in Why it matters and Governance controls.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to use Microsoft Purview eDiscovery, but the controls table has no eDiscovery row.
claims.quote: use the Thread ID to find the conversation in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery ... Controls rows: Viewing and exporting security detections in Teams; Weaponizable File Protection.
claims.fix: Remove 'use the Thread ID to find the conversation in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery' from the After rollout checklist, deleting the bullet if no text remains after the external-sender correction. Keep the supported explanation of Thread ID in Why it matters.

claims.claim: Users see no change from the report.
claims.quote: Searched: Security detections report Teams automatically available enable report setting retention licensing. Read report and roadmap: they describe an administrator report but do not explicitly establish that users see no change.
claims.fix: Replace 'users see no change, although recipients named in the report can be identified by admins' with 'the report displays sender and recipient information for administrators'.
